tokyo_asaba.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. 阿娑縛 has no website and no menu registered on Tabelog (the /dtlmenu/ page falls through to the shop top page). Everything below was read off PHOTOGRAPHS of the shop's own menu book, shot 2025/08, at full resolution: the soba spread (cold and hot), the sashimi/tempura page, and a separate seasonal insert sheet. Prices on the card are written in kanji numerals (一三〇〇 = ¥1,300). A second photo set from 2026/06 shows the handwritten daily slips clipped to a stand on the counter, which is where the duck and chicken dishes and the seasonal vegetables live — those five are dated 2026/06 and are the freshest figures here. Some lines on both the card and the slips are STRUCK OUT (焼き車えび and one further sashimi line on the printed card; a 鴨もも焼 ¥2,600 line on the daily slip) — those are recorded only as unavailable, not as items. Where a price could not be read with certainty it is left empty rather than guessed. Shop confirmed as 東京都台東区浅草1-24-3 橋口ビル1F, 2 min from Asakusa (Tsukuba Express); evenings only, 17:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:00), closed Mondays; Tabelog's diner-reported budget band is ¥8,000–9,999, i.e. this is a soba-and-sake house, not a quick noodle stop. NO ALLERGEN INFORMATION IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE. Nothing here is safe for coeliac disease: it is a soba kitchen with a tempura fryer, and every 汁 is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Seiro — chilled soba on a slatted tray with dipping tsuyu. The plain benchmark order.
items.note: The card does not state the buckwheat-to-wheat ratio, so assume a wheat blend. Even a 100% buckwheat noodle would fail here: 打ち粉 dusting flour, a boiling pot shared with wheat noodles, and a tsuyu of katsuo dashi plus wheat-brewed soy sauce. Bonito dashi also rules out vegan.

items.en: Cold soba with grated mountain yam
items.note: The yam is plant-only; the noodle and the dashi-and-soy tsuyu are not.

items.en: Cold soba with tempura
items.note: Wheat noodle, wheat tempura batter, soy tsuyu, and a fryer shared with everything else on the tempura page.

items.en: Hana soba — the shop's own named soba. A diner photo of it shows a lacquer bowl of soba under a heavy scatter of a crumbled brown topping, served with a small side dish; the card itself gives no description and the shop publishes none, so what is on it is not recorded here.
items.note: Price cross-checked twice: ¥1,600 on the menu card and 1,600円(税込) on the shop's own photo-and-caption sheet. Wheat-blend noodle and soy tsuyu regardless of the topping. Ask what the topping is before ordering on any restricted diet — nobody has published it.

items.en: Suzushiro soba — cold soba with daikon (suzushiro is the classical name for the radish, one of the seven herbs of spring)
items.note: The card gives the name only, not the preparation, so how the daikon is cut or dressed is unknown. Wheat-blend noodle and wheat soy tsuyu either way.

items.en: Cold soba with sesame
items.note: A sesame dipping sauce in a soba shop is the house tsuyu (soy sauce and dashi) loosened with ground sesame. Wheat and bonito.

items.en: Cold soba with sharp grated daikon
items.note: Wheat-blend noodle, soy-and-dashi tsuyu.

items.en: Tanuki tsuke soba — cold soba with a dipping broth carrying tempura crumbs. Named in a 2026 diner's own list of what the shop does well.
items.note: たぬき means 天かす — loose fried TEMPURA BATTER, which is pure wheat. This is the most explicitly wheat-loaded soba on the card, on top of the wheat-blend noodle and the soy tsuyu.

items.en: Cold soba with fermented soybeans
items.note: Natto is fermented soybean and is itself plant-only, but the sachet of tare that comes with it is soy-sauce and bonito based, and so is the soba tsuyu. Natto sets usually include a raw egg or karashi too.

items.en: Kake soba — hot soba in dashi broth
items.note: Wheat-blend noodle in bonito dashi seasoned with wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Hot soba with tempura
items.note: Wheat noodle, wheat batter, soy broth.

items.en: Hot soba under soft-set egg
items.note: Egg, soy broth, wheat-blend noodle.

items.en: Okame soba — hot soba arranged with an assortment of toppings (the Tokyo classic: kamaboko fish cake, shiitake, greens and so on, laid out to suggest a face)
items.note: The card names the dish only. In the standard Tokyo composition every element is a wheat risk: kamaboko is bound with starch and often wheat, the shiitake and kanpyo are simmered in soy sauce, and the broth is soy. Fish cake and dashi rule out vegan.

items.en: Hot soba with shiitake mushrooms
items.note: Shiitake in a soba shop are simmered in soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Wheat via the soy, bonito via the broth.

items.en: Hot soba with aosa sea lettuce
items.note: Aosa is a green seaweed — plant-only in itself — but it sits in the shop's bonito-and-soy broth on a wheat-blend noodle.

items.en: Curry nanban — hot soba in a curry-thickened dashi broth with spring onion
items.note: A soba shop's curry nanban is made by thickening its dashi-and-soy broth with Japanese curry powder or roux, and Japanese curry roux is a WHEAT-FLOUR roux. Wheat three ways: noodle, soy sauce, roux.

items.en: Bonito sashimi
items.note: Raw fish, so never vegan. The fish itself carries no wheat — the wheat is in the soy sauce it is served with, and possibly in a ponzu or a moromi-style dipping miso. This is the section a wheat-avoider should look at, but only after establishing what it is dipped in; carry gluten-free tamari or ask for salt.

items.en: Horse mackerel sashimi
items.note: Same as the bonito: the fish is clean, the soy sauce is not. Read off the card as 六五〇 — much the cheapest sashimi on the page.

items.en: White squid sashimi
items.note: Squid. Wheat risk sits entirely in the dipping soy sauce.

items.en: Splendid alfonsino (kinmedai) sashimi
items.note: Fish. Wheat risk is the soy sauce it is dipped in.

items.en: Octopus sliced paper-thin
items.note: Octopus. Usu-zukuri is normally served with ponzu rather than plain soy — ponzu is citrus plus soy sauce, so still wheat unless the shop says otherwise. Ask.

items.en: Octopus cut into chunks
items.note: Boiled octopus in bite-size pieces, eaten with soy sauce or wasabi-soy. The wheat is the soy.

items.en: Whole dried sardines, grilled
items.note: Sardines salted, dried whole and grilled — no batter, no sauce required, which makes this one of the more promising plates on the card for a wheat-avoider. But the shop publishes no ingredient information, the grill is shared, and it is usually served with a wedge of citrus and soy. Ask.

items.en: Grilled squid legs
items.note: Geso-yaki is brushed with a soy-sauce-and-mirin tare on the grill, or served with soy mayonnaise. Wheat via the soy.

items.en: Soba miso — miso mixed with roasted buckwheat groats and grilled, the classic soba-shop plate to drink over. Named by a 2026 diner as one of the shop's good ones.
items.note: THIS ONE LOOKS SAFE AND IS NOT. The buckwheat groats are fine, but miso is the problem: 麦味噌 (barley miso) and blended miso are both normal in this dish, barley is gluten, and — unlike wheat — barley is NOT on Japan's statutory allergen labelling list, so nothing has to declare it. Soba miso is also usually loosened with mirin and sometimes sake or dashi. On the vegan side, miso and buckwheat are plant-only but bonito dashi is often stirred in; ask.

items.en: Yanaka ginger — young stem ginger eaten raw with miso
items.note: The card is written in cursive and the trailing characters run together, but the item is Yanaka-style young ginger. The ginger is plant-only; the miso it is dipped in is the gluten question (barley miso is common and undeclared) and may be a moromi or dashi-enriched miso, which would also break vegan. Ask.

items.en: Salt-grilled ebodai (Japanese butterfish)
items.note: From the seasonal insert sheet, so it may not be on every night. NO PRICE IS RECORDED because the kanji numeral on the photographed sheet could not be read with certainty — ask at the counter rather than trusting a number nobody could see. Salt-grilled whole fish with no sauce is among the better bets for a wheat-avoider, but nothing is published and the grill is shared.

items.en: Chilled tomato
items.note: Chilled tomato, cut and served cold. Plant-only as an ingredient and the closest thing on this card to a vegan plate — but Japanese izakaya tomato is very often served with a dressing or a scoop of mayonnaise, and neither the card nor the shop says which. Ask for it plain.

items.en: Cucumber with spicy moromi miso
items.section: 本日のおすすめ Daily specials (handwritten slips, 2026/06)
items.note: A GLUTEN TRAP HIDING IN A PLATE OF CUCUMBER. もろみ (moromi) is the fermentation mash from SOY SAUCE brewing, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed from soybeans AND WHEAT in roughly equal parts — moromi miso therefore contains wheat by construction, not by accident. The cucumber is fine; the dip is not. Vegan is a separate open question: moromi miso is often enriched with bonito or fish. From the 2026/06 daily slip.

items.en: Maitake mushroom tempura. One serving.

items.en: Juwari soba — chilled 100% buckwheat soba, stone-milled and hand-cut by the fourth-generation owner. Limited quantity. Large portion +¥450.

items.en: Extra dipping tsuyu

items.en: Sesame dipping-broth soba with pork — lunch only, limited daily quantity. Choose no-heat or spicy; Hara Ryokaku black shichimi is recommended alongside. The egg comes on a separate dish — stir it into the dipping broth to mellow it.

tokyo_thai_garden_shibuya.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Taken from the shop's OWN 公式 (owner-managed) Tabelog listing — 86 dishes with the shop's own Japanese, Thai-transliterated and English names and its own 辛味 (chilli) 1–3 scale — 更新日 2024/07/02, tax included. Two years old, so treat the figures as a guide; the shop's own domain thaigardenspice.com no longer resolves (connection fails on http and https, with and without www), so there is no newer first-party list to check against. Address confirmed 渋谷区宇田川町24-10 B1, Shibuya Center-gai, open daily, 74 seats. The shop's own listing states 「ベジタリアンメニューあり」 — VEGETARIAN, which in a Thai kitchen does not mean vegan: fish sauce (ナンプラー) and shrimp paste are in most curry pastes, dressings and stir-fry seasonings, so ask specifically for 'no fish sauce, no shrimp paste' rather than 'vegetarian'. Beyond the 86 dishes below the listing also counts 73 drinks, 18 lunch items and 4 courses (from ¥3,300; a ¥4,950 course drops to ¥4,400 with the Tabelog coupon; 2-hour all-you-can-drink ¥2,178 per person from 4 people) — those sub-tabs are not retrievable, so no drink or lunch prices are recorded here. NO ALLERGEN CHART IS PUBLISHED. Every gf value below is reasoning from named ingredients, not from a shop statement.

items.en: Khao kha mu — the stewed pork leg served over rice
items.note: Same soy-braised pork leg, on rice. Wheat via the braising soy sauce.

items.en: Stir-fried bean sprouts and thick fried tofu
items.note: The ingredients named are all plant — bean sprouts and deep-fried tofu — which makes this one of the two most promising dishes on the card for a vegan. But a Thai stir-fry is seasoned by default with fish sauce and oyster sauce (oyster sauce commonly contains wheat), and the shop publishes nothing. Ask for it made with soy/salt only and no nam pla.

items.en: Meatballs with sweet chilli sauce
items.note: Meat, so not vegan. Meatballs are usually bound with flour or breadcrumb and Thai sweet chilli sauce, though normally wheat-free, is not documented here. Ask.

items.en: Gyoza, five pieces — the shop's own filling. Also tom yum gyoza ¥836 and coriander gyoza ¥836, each five pieces, all served with a special dipping sauce

items.ja: 生春巻（ポーピアソッド）

items.note: Fresh spring rolls are wrapped in rice paper rather than wheat, and are not fried, so they avoid two of this kitchen's wheat routes — but the filling normally contains prawn or pork and the dipping sauce is the open question (Thai plum or sweet chilli sauce is usually wheat-free; a hoisin-style peanut sauce is not). Ask about both wrapper and sauce.

items.ja: タイ風卵焼き（カイジョウ ムゥ/クン）
items.en: Thai omelette with minced pork ¥1,078 or prawn ¥1,210
items.note: Egg and meat, so never vegan. A Thai omelette is egg seasoned with fish sauce and deep-fried in a wok of oil — the fryer oil is shared with battered items here, and rice flour is sometimes added for crispness. Ask.

items.ja: 揚げ生春巻（ポーピアトーサワン）
items.en: Deep-fried spring rolls. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: Fried spring-roll pastry is wheat, and it goes through the shared fryer.

items.ja: 海老トースト（カノムパンナートム）
items.en: Fried minced-prawn toast. Marked 定番.
items.note: It is literally bread — sliced wheat loaf spread with prawn paste and deep-fried.

items.en: Deep-fried fish cakes
items.note: Fish. Thai tod man is fish paste bound with red curry paste and egg and normally contains no wheat flour — but it is deep-fried in the same oil as the spring rolls and prawn toast, which is a cross-contamination route on its own. Not recommended for coeliac.

items.ja: 海老のさつま揚げ（トーマンクン）2ヶ
items.en: Deep-fried prawn cakes, two pieces
items.note: Prawn cakes are usually coated in breadcrumbs before frying, and the fryer is shared with wheat items regardless.

items.ja: 海老春巻き（ポーピアンクントース）
items.en: Fried prawn spring rolls
items.note: Wheat spring-roll pastry, shared fryer, prawn.

items.ja: 揚げ春巻き（ポーピアトース）
items.en: Fried vegetable spring rolls
items.note: Wheat pastry — the wrapper alone rules it out for coeliac. The filling is glass noodle and vegetables and may well be vegan, but Thai spring-roll filling often carries minced pork or fish sauce, and the pastry is usually egg-sealed. Ask.

items.ja: 鶏のなんこつ揚げ（エンガイトース）
items.en: Deep-fried chicken cartilage
items.note: Deep-fried chicken is flour- or batter-coated, in a shared fryer.

items.ja: 鶏肉とレモングラス揚げ（ガイタカイ）
items.en: Chicken deep-fried with lemongrass
items.note: Flour coating and shared fryer; the marinade is normally soy- and oyster-sauce based.

items.ja: ソフトシェルのピリ辛揚げ（プーンムプリックァー）
items.en: Soft-shell crab fried with chilli. Chilli level 1.
items.note: Flour-dusted and deep-fried; chilli jam is often soy-seasoned. Crab.

items.ja: 海老のガーリック揚げ（クントーガティーム）
items.en: Prawns deep-fried with garlic
items.note: Deep-fried prawn, shared fryer, soy-and-oyster garlic sauce.

items.ja: 揚げ魚のタイソースかけ（プラーラペック）
items.en: Whole deep-fried fish under a spicy Thai sauce. Chilli level 3. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: The fish is flour-dusted and deep-fried, and rad prik sauce is fish sauce, tamarind, palm sugar and usually oyster and soy sauce.

items.ja: 揚げ魚のイサーンソース（プラトーナムトックム）
items.en: Deep-fried fish with spicy Isaan dressing. Chilli level 3.
items.note: Flour-dusted and deep-fried; Isaan dressing is fish sauce, lime, chilli and toasted rice powder.

items.en: Tom yum goong — hot-and-sour prawn soup with lemongrass, galangal and lime leaf. Chilli level 2.
items.note: Prawn and fish sauce, so not vegan. Tom yum is structurally wheat-free — herbs, chilli, lime, fish sauce — but Thai kitchens routinely add chilli jam (nam prik pao) and seasoning sauce, and no allergen line is published. Ask.

items.ja: 鶏肉のココナッツスープ（トムカーガイ）
items.en: Tom kha gai — chicken in a sour coconut-milk soup with galangal. Chilli level 2. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: Chicken and fish sauce. Coconut milk, galangal, lemongrass and lime are wheat-free; the fish sauce and any seasoning sauce are the open question. Ask.

items.ja: シーフードとハーブのクリアトムヤムスープ（トムヤムポーテック）
items.en: Po taek — clear hot-and-sour seafood soup with herbs. Chilli level 2.
items.note: Seafood and fish sauce. Clear (no coconut milk), so fewer added ingredients — but the seasoning sauce question stands. Ask.

items.ja: 豆腐と卵のスープ（ゲーンチュー）
items.en: Gaeng jued — mild clear soup with tofu and egg
items.note: Egg rules out vegan, and gaeng jued's stock is pork bone seasoned with soy sauce and often has minced pork in it. Wheat via the soy.

items.ja: タイ風焼きそば（パッタイ）
items.en: Pad thai — stir-fried flat rice noodles with tamarind, egg, bean sprouts and crushed peanut. Marked 定番.
items.note: The noodle is rice, which is the good news. But pad thai sauce is tamarind, palm sugar and FISH SAUCE, with dried shrimp and egg in the wok — not vegan — and many kitchens add soy or seasoning sauce to it. Ask whether soy sauce goes in.

items.ja: タイスキ焼きそば（スキヘン）
items.en: Suki haeng — 'dry' Thai-suki stir-fried noodles. Chilli level 2.
items.note: Thai suki sauce is a fermented-bean-curd and soy-sauce sauce. Egg and meat or seafood in the wok.

items.ja: 太麺焼きそば（パッシーユー）
items.en: Pad see ew — wide flat rice noodles stir-fried with Chinese broccoli and egg. The shop's own English line reads 'fried wide noodles soy sauce taste'.
items.note: The dish is NAMED after the sauce: ซีอิ๊ว / see ew IS soy sauce, and the shop's own description says so. Thai dark and light soy sauce are wheat-brewed. Egg too. A rice noodle in a wheat sauce is exactly the trap this list exists to catch.

items.ja: 海老入りスパイシー太麺焼きそば（パッキーマオ）
items.en: Drunken noodles — wide rice noodles stir-fried with seafood, holy basil and chilli. Chilli level 3.
items.note: Rice noodle, but the sauce is soy sauce, oyster sauce and fish sauce. Seafood.

items.ja: 豚肉のあんかけ太麺（クイティオラットナームゥ）
items.en: Rad na — wide rice noodles under a thick pork-and-vegetable gravy
items.note: The gravy is fermented soybean sauce and oyster sauce thickened with starch, poured over noodles that were first charred in soy sauce. Pork.

items.ja: タイスキ春雨（スキナム）
items.en: Suki nam — glass noodles in Thai-suki broth. Chilli level 1.
items.note: Mung-bean noodles, but the suki sauce is fermented bean curd and soy sauce, and the broth is meat-based with egg.

items.ja: トムヤムクンライスヌードル（クイッティオトムヤムクン）
items.en: Tom yum goong rice noodles. Chilli level 2.
items.note: Rice noodle in a tom yum broth — prawn and fish sauce (not vegan). Thai noodle-soup broths are usually seasoned with soy or seasoning sauce, so the wheat question is real. Ask.

items.ja: ココナッツカレーヌードル（カオソーイ）
items.en: Khao soi — northern Thai coconut curry noodles. Chilli level 1. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: Khao soi is made with EGG NOODLES — wheat — and is topped with a nest of the same noodles deep-fried. The curry also carries soy sauce and the dish comes with chicken. Wheat twice.

items.ja: タイ風チキンライスヌードル（クイッティオガイ）
items.en: Rice noodles with chicken, Thai style
items.note: Rice noodle, chicken broth. The broth's seasoning (soy vs fish sauce) is undocumented. Ask.

items.ja: タイ風ポークライスヌードル（クイッティオトムヤム）
items.en: Rice noodles with pork in a hot-and-sour dressing
items.note: Rice noodle, pork. Seasoning undocumented — ask about soy and seasoning sauce.

items.ja: 煮込みビーフライスヌードル（クイッティオヌァトゥン）
items.en: Rice noodles with slow-stewed beef. Marked 人気 (popular).
items.note: Rice noodle, but Thai stewed-beef broth is braised with dark soy sauce and five-spice. Wheat via the soy. Beef.

items.ja: 鶏肉のバジル炒めご飯目玉焼きのせ（ガパオガイラートカオ）
items.en: Pad kaphrao over rice with a fried egg on top — chicken ¥1,320 / pork ¥1,430 / beef ¥1,650. Chilli level 2. Marked 定番.
items.note: Same kaphrao sauce as the stir-fry: soy sauce and oyster sauce, both wheat routes. Egg and meat.

items.ja: グリーンカレーチャーハン（カオパッキョウワン）
items.en: Green curry fried rice. Chilli level 1.
items.note: Thai fried rice is seasoned with soy sauce; green curry paste normally contains shrimp paste. Wheat and shellfish.

items.ja: トムヤムクンチャーハン（カオパットムヤムクン）
items.en: Tom yum goong fried rice. Chilli level 2. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: Fried rice is soy-seasoned; prawn and fish sauce.

items.ja: タイ風海老チャーハン（カオパックン）
items.en: Thai prawn fried rice
items.note: Soy sauce and fish sauce are the standard seasoning for khao phat; egg and prawn.

items.ja: タイ風チキンライス（カオマンガイ）
items.en: Khao man gai — poached chicken with rice cooked in the chicken broth. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: The chicken and rice themselves are wheat-free, but khao man gai is defined by its sauce — fermented soybean paste (taochiao) with ginger, chilli and soy sauce — and the accompanying clear soup is soy-seasoned. Ask for it with no sauce and you are still relying on the rice's cooking liquid. Chicken.

items.ja: 豚肉のチャーハン（カオパッムー）
items.en: Thai pork fried rice
items.note: Soy- and fish-sauce seasoned, with egg and pork.

items.ja: パイナップルチャーハン（カオオッサッパロス）
items.en: Fried rice with prawn served in a hollowed fresh pineapple. Marked 定番.
items.note: Soy-seasoned fried rice with prawn, egg, raisins and cashew.

items.ja: ジャスミンライス（カオフォムマリ）
items.en: Plain steamed jasmine rice
items.note: Steamed jasmine rice and water — no wheat, no animal product, no sauce, and it does not go near the wok or the fryer. It is served on its own plate, so the only realistic risk is a shared serving spoon. This is the survival order in a Thai kitchen for a coeliac.

items.en: Steamed sticky rice, the Isaan staple
items.note: Glutinous rice is rice — the word 'glutinous' describes the texture, NOT gluten, and it contains no wheat protein at all. Steamed in a basket with nothing added; no animal ingredient.

items.ja: グリーンカレー（ゲーン・キョウワーン）
items.en: Green curry with chicken ¥1,045 / pork ¥1,155 / beef ¥1,375. Chilli level 2. Marked 定番.
items.note: Meat and fish sauce, and green curry paste normally contains shrimp paste (kapi) — so not vegan under any substitution short of the kitchen making a separate paste. Thai curry paste and coconut milk are structurally wheat-free, which makes the curries the most promising section here for a wheat-avoider, but the paste brand and any added seasoning sauce are undocumented. Ask.

items.ja: イエローカレー（ゲーン・カリー）
items.en: Yellow curry with chicken ¥1,045 / pork ¥1,155 / beef ¥1,375
items.note: Not a Japanese roux curry — this is a Thai coconut curry, so no wheat flour thickener. Fish sauce and shrimp paste in the base; meat on top. Ask about seasoning sauce.

items.ja: レッドココナッツカレー（ゲーン・パネーン）
items.en: Panang — thick red coconut curry with chicken ¥1,045 or pork ¥1,155. Chilli level 1.
items.note: Coconut cream and red curry paste with peanut; the paste normally carries shrimp paste and the dish is finished with fish sauce. Wheat unlikely but unconfirmed — ask.

items.ja: 揚げ海老のココナッツカレーソース（シューシークン）
items.en: Deep-fried prawns in a choo chee coconut curry sauce
items.note: The prawns are battered and deep-fried before saucing — the coating and the shared fryer are the wheat, not the curry.

items.ja: マッサマンカレー（ゲーン・マッサマン）
items.en: Massaman — mild coconut curry with chicken, potato, peanuts and warm spices. The shop's line: 'No.1 food of the world in CNN'. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: Chicken; massaman paste normally contains shrimp paste and the curry is finished with fish sauce and tamarind. No wheat ingredient in the classic recipe, but nothing is published. Ask.

items.ja: 揚げバナナ春巻きのココナッツアイス添え（クルイートードアイティム）
items.en: Fried banana spring roll with coconut ice cream
items.note: Wheat spring-roll pastry through the shared fryer. Coconut ice cream may or may not contain dairy — this one is not documented, so the dessert fails on the pastry regardless.

items.ja: 焼きプリンとココナッツアイス添え（モーケンアイティム）
items.en: Baked Thai custard with coconut ice cream. Marked 人気.
items.note: Khanom mo kaeng is coconut milk, palm sugar, mung-bean or taro and DUCK EGG — never vegan. Traditionally wheat-free (no flour), but the ice cream and any base are undocumented. Ask. Plain baked custard 焼きプリン ¥638.

items.ja: マンゴープリン（マンモプニン）
items.en: Mango pudding
items.note: A set pudding — the setting agent decides everything. GELATIN (animal) and agar (plant) are both common in Japanese-Thai kitchens, and dairy cream is usual in mango pudding. Neither is documented. Ask on both counts. Served with coconut ice cream and sticky rice for ¥1,430.

items.ja: ういろう風ココナッツミルク餅
items.en: Coconut-milk pudding, Thai style — layered and chewy like uiro
items.note: Thai layered coconut sweets are made from rice, tapioca and mung-bean flour with coconut milk, which would be both wheat-free and dairy-free — but the shop names no ingredients and 'uiro-style' could also mean a wheat-flour version. Ask.

items.ja: ココナッツプリン（カノムトゥアイ）
items.en: Khanom tuay — steamed coconut custard in a little cup
items.note: Classic khanom tuay is rice flour, coconut milk and palm sugar — no wheat, no dairy, no egg — which makes it the most likely vegan dessert on the card. Unconfirmed by the shop, so ask.

items.ja: タピオカココナッツミルク（サクー）
items.en: Tapioca pearls in coconut milk. Marked 定番.
items.note: Tapioca is cassava starch and coconut milk is plant — structurally this is both wheat-free and dairy-free. Nothing is published to confirm it, so ask. With coconut ice cream added ¥748.

items.ja: タイ風おしるこ（ブァロイ）
items.en: Bua loi — glutinous rice-flour dumplings in sweet coconut soup. Marked おすすめ.
items.note: Despite the Japanese name おしるこ this is the Thai dessert: dumplings of GLUTINOUS RICE flour (rice, not wheat — the name misleads) in coconut milk. Often served with a poached egg in Thailand, which would break vegan. Ask whether egg is included and whether any wheat flour is in the dough.

items.en: Tofu under ground sesame

items.en: Rice-bran pickles
items.note: ぬか漬 is pickled in a rice-bran bed — rice bran itself is not a gluten grain, but nukadoko is often started with beer or barley and pickles are frequently finished with soy sauce. Ask.

items.en: Kimchi

The もんじゃ section is transcribed from a photograph of the shop's own printed グランドメニュー taken 2026/04 and those figures are current. Everything else — okonomiyaki, teppanyaki, otsumami, rice, dessert, drinks — comes from the shop's own HotPepper page (もんじゃ浅吉 本店, strJ003365820, address 東京都台東区浅草2-14-11, matching the record), which is shop-maintained but was last updated 更新日 2022/09/19 (drinks 2022/09/20). Two monja on the 2022 page (鴨ねぎもんじゃ ¥1,380, シーチキンもんじゃ ¥880) do NOT appear on the 2026 card and are not listed here rather than being carried forward as if current. The Tabelog menu tab holds no registered items at all. The shop publishes NO allergen information anywhere — not on HotPepper, not on Instagram, not in the photographed card — so every gf/vegan flag is reasoning from the shop's own printed ingredient lists and from what monja unavoidably is, never a shop claim. In gluten terms this is one of the least survivable rooms in Tokyo: the batter is wheat, the griddle is the table, and every dish including the steaks and the fried rice is cooked in that batter's residue.

items.en: The house mixed monja — raw squid, sakura shrimp, dried shredded squid, corn, chikuwa fish cake, fish sausage, coarse pork, red pickled ginger, yakisoba noodles and tenkasu
items.note: The card prints the full filling list: 生いか・桜えび・きりいか・コーン・ちくわ・魚肉ソーセージ・豚粗・紅しょうが・そば・揚玉. Monja and okonomiyaki are a WHEAT-FLOUR batter cooked on the table griddle — there is no gluten-free version of this dish anywhere in this shop. The shop's own HotPepper copy adds a second wheat route: 「自家製の出汁で味付けされた生地」, the batter is seasoned with the house dashi, and a Japanese dashi is normally built on 白だし / めんつゆ / だし醤油, all soy-sauce based and therefore wheat. That dashi is also the vegan problem before you reach the egg and seafood. Note too that 「そば」 in a monja shop means Chinese-style WHEAT noodles (yakisoba), not buckwheat, and 揚玉 (tenkasu) is fried wheat batter. Marked おすすめ on the card.

tokyo_woodberry_bakery.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included figures transcribed from the shop's OWN branch menu PDFs, linked from woodberrycoffee.com/pages/menu under the BAKERY heading: 260805_BAKERY_FOOD.pdf (file dated 2026-08-05) and 2608_BAKERY_DRINK.pdf. Both were cross-checked against photographs of the physical card on the table and the counter board, shot 2026-03 and 2026-04, and every overlapping price agrees, which is why the confidence is high. THE SHOP'S OWN PDF DISAGREES WITH ITSELF, and this record follows the newer figure: its first page (a summary sheet carrying the morning set) prices エッグベネディクト and アボカドトースト at ¥1,870 and the acai bowl at ¥1,960, while the booklet pages behind it and both in-store photographs say ¥1,970, ¥1,970 and ¥1,980. クロックマダム ¥1,670 appears ONLY on that stale-looking summary page and on neither counter card — treat it as the least reliable line here. TWO ITEMS COME FROM THE IN-STORE CARD AND NOT THE PDF: 季節のクレープ ¥1,980 and the 季節のスープとパンのセット ¥1,320 were on the counter board photographed 2026-03; the seasonal slots rotate (the 2026-04 booklet's seasonal crepe was フォレ・ノワール; the current PDF replaces the slot with ティラミスフレンチトースト ¥1,650), and the grilled tuna sandwich's vegetable changed from asparagus in April to 菜の花 on the current sheet. The ハンドドリップ line is on the in-store card with 「PLEASE ASK US」 where the price should be, so it is recorded with no price rather than a guess. THE BAKERY-COUNTER PASTRIES ARE A DIFFERENT VINTAGE AND ARE MARKED AS SUCH: the four 焼き菓子 with prices (¥770 × 3, ¥460) come from the shop's own opening announcement, which stamps them 「2024年5月20日現在」. The case rotates; those four are recorded because they are the only ones the shop has ever described in writing, and because one of them carries the gluten-free claim. GLUTEN, PLAINLY: this is a BAKERY. The house bread is 自家製天然酵母と国産有機小麦のカンパーニュ and, per the shop, 有機小麦とライ麦と古代小麦のスペルト全粒粉 — wheat, rye and spelt — plus bagels and shokupan. Every sandwich, toast, lunch plate and french toast is built on it. NOTHING on this record is flagged ‘gf’, including the tarte tatin the shop itself calls ヴィーガン＆グルテンフリー and the 米粉 florentine: those are recipe claims made inside a working wheat bakery, and the shop makes no separate-equipment, separate-room or no-contamination claim anywhere on its site. The honest label for a coeliac is ‘ask, and show a coeliac card’. VEGAN, BY CONTRAST, IS GENUINELY WELL SERVED and the shop says so itself: the concept line on its own location page is 「地球にも身体にも優しいがコンセプトのベーカリー。ヴィーガンやグルテンフリーなどのヘルスコンシャスなレシピの焼き菓子とパンをご提供するベーカリーカフェです」. There is a named vegan sandwich, a vegan crepe, vegan ice cream, an all-plant acai bowl, and soy (+¥50) or oat (+¥100) milk on every espresso drink. The shop publishes NO allergen chart — no アレルギー or 特定原材料 page exists on the site, and the FAQ does not mention allergens — so every flag here is reasoned from the ingredient lines the shop prints under each dish, and those lines are summaries, not full recipes. Hours are 9:00–18:00 with 定休日あり (LO food 17:00, drink 18:00) per the shop's location page; the morning set is 9:00–11:00 only. The 2024 opening announcement's 11:00–18:00 is out of date. Address confirmed 東京都渋谷区東2-18-7 on both the shop's site and Tabelog — the same Higashi 2-chome block as WOODBERRY COFFEE 渋谷店 (2-20-18), which is a DIFFERENT shop with a different menu; do not merge them. Tabelog has no registered menu for this listing (the /dtlmenu/ URL falls through to the shop top page).
